name: greppy-help
stdout:
Code navigation for coding agents, with byte-exact real-grep passthrough for ordinary grep invocations.

Usage: greppy [OPTIONS] [PASSTHROUGH]... [COMMAND]

Commands:
  prompt          Export the complete embedded prompt with version and hashes
  index           Index a repository
  where-am-i      The repository at one glance: layout, languages, entry points, test roots
  cache           Inspect or safely reclaim Greppy-managed cache data
  agent           Manage persisted agent proposals
  workspace       Install, inspect and maintain the portable CoW provider
  trial           Run one isolated own-project baseline/Greppy observation with Pi
  search-graph    Structured graph search
  trace           Call-graph trace
  impact          Impact / blast-radius — the TRANSITIVE set reachable from `S` over one edge type, with hop distance, in ONE call. `--direction incoming` (default) answers "if I change S, what breaks?" (all transitive callers); `--direction outgoing` answers "what does S ultimately reach?". Replaces a dozen iterative who-calls/callees an agent would otherwise run
  brief           Sketch the body of a function: its doc sentence, the verbatim signature head, then one line per call site or branch naming the real symbol used there — followed by the aggregated callers and, when the call tree below is worth it, an expand offer. Structs, enums and traits have no body to sketch: they print their whole definition. This is the orientation aid; `who-calls` and `callees` give addresses
  bash-smart      Run a command untouched and fold long output behind an expand id
  expand          Print a prepared evidence pack created by a previous query command. Global --offset/--limit select saved raw lines. --max-bytes reserves metadata (1024 bytes text, 2048 JSON) and never splits a raw line; one oversized line is emitted whole with explicit evidence
  read            Print symbol definitions as source bytes, including documentation and attributes immediately above each definition
  read-smart      Print symbol definitions with nested structural blocks folded into semantic one-line gaps that can be expanded recursively
  read-file       Read files directly, in 400-line pages unless a range or all lines were requested
  replace         Replace a definition with NEW; without NEW, read it from stdin
  replace-text    Replace OLD in F; OLD must occur exactly once unless --expect says otherwise
  replace-lines   Replace inclusive 1-based lines A:B in F
  replace-span    Replace the byte-exact span named by H
  write           Create or overwrite PATH with NEW
  delete          Remove a definition
  delete-lines    Remove inclusive 1-based lines A:B from F
  insert-lines    Insert NEW after line N in F; line 0 means the top
  rename          Rename a definition and every graph-resolved reference
  undo            Reverse an edit; without ID, reverse the latest one
  patch           Apply a unified diff to existing files as one transaction
  stats           Print deterministic graph statistics for the workspace project: file count, node counts by label, edge counts by type, and the node/edge totals
  diagnostics     Store/index diagnostics: schema health, integrity check, workspace state, graph stats and provider completeness
  doctor          End-to-end health check for the active workspace index
  who-calls       Who calls or uses `S` — incoming CALLS and USAGE edges, printed as `qualified_name file:line`. With `--code`, also prints each caller's source span so the agent reads the body without a separate file Read
  callees         Resolved indexed definitions called by `S` — direct outgoing CALLS edges, printed as `qualified_name file:line`. External or unresolved calls are not included; an empty answer does not prove the source has no calls. Use `greppy read S` for source. With `--code`, also prints each resolved callee's source span
  fan-in          Top symbols by incoming edge degree. Default edge type is CALLS, so this shows the most-called symbols in the current project
  fan-out         Top symbols by outgoing edge degree. Default edge type is CALLS, so this shows the symbols that directly call the most other symbols
  graph-locate    Locate the innermost indexed graph symbol enclosing a grep-style `file:line` location. Accepts either `graph-locate src/lib.rs:42` or `graph-locate --file src/lib.rs --line 42`
  path            Show every call chain between two symbols as one tree of call sites. The start is printed at its definition; each indented child is the editable site in its parent that calls the named symbol
  search-pattern  Every source line matching a regular expression
  search-symbol   Definitions whose name contains NAME
  plus            Fused search: combine literal/full-text, symbol, fuzzy semantic, and graph-neighbour signals into grep-like ranked hits. This is search output, not a generated answer: each row stays `file:line score signals symbol snippet`
  search          Definitions that do what a plain-English query describes
  web             Experimental web runtime. Not a production Playwright compatibility claim

Arguments:
  [PASSTHROUGH]...  Trailing positional / flag arguments used as a passthrough when no recognised subcommand matched. clap captures here whatever remains after subcommand parsing

Options:
      --root <ROOT>
          Explicit repository root (RV-006). When set, `index` and every query subcommand (search-graph / trace / search-pattern / search-symbol / search) key the on-disk store and the project identity on this path instead of detecting the repo root by walking up from the current directory. `global = true` lets it be passed either before or after the subcommand: grep --root /repo search-pattern foo grep search-pattern --root /repo foo
      --device <auto|cpu|metal|cuda[:INDEX]>
          Native inference backend for both embedded models
      --no-gpu
          Legacy spelling for `--device cpu`
      --limit <N>
          Cap the number of rows returned by navigation and search commands. `--max` is an alias; `--all` lifts default caps but preserves an explicit --limit
      --max-bytes <N>
          Hard stdout payload budget for navigation, search, read, and human web views. Result rows/content are trimmed before status and continuation metadata
      --offset <N>
          Continue a budgeted navigation, search, or read result at row N [default: 0]
      --diagnostics
          Restore the full machine-readable diagnostics envelope for `--json`. Default JSON carries only the answer, counts, and actionable warnings
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version

Agent modes:
  greppy agent ["INITIAL TASK"] --model MODEL   Interactive TUI
  greppy -p "TASK" --model MODEL                Headless one-shot
publication_note: Secret redaction; unvalidated model IDs/catalogs and unrelated commands omitted. Runtime scripts rediscover selections.
